Subject: Clarification on metering for nested-document workflows

Hi Dylan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — our engineering team liked the latency and prefix caching behavior. Before we start the 30-day pilot, procurement asked a couple of billing clarifications that I couldn't find in the docs. Two quick items: 

1) We pass nested documents to the model (an outer patient summary plus up to 10 historical notes embedded as a JSON array). Are those treated as one request for context-length purposes or do we get charged per nested element if the runtime expands them into separate KV cache entries?

2) For pilot pricing, what rounding/miniimum rules apply to streaming responses? If a chat stream sends small heartbeat requests (empty prompt with only metadata) during a session, do those incur the session minimum or is there a per-call floor?

I've attached a small sample of the payloads we plan to send. Can you loop in someone from engineering on the billing side? Procurement needs the answers to finalize the SOW.

Thanks,
Eli

Subject: Re: Clarification on metering for nested-document workflows

Eli — thanks for the sample, that helps. Short answers up front, then I'll let Sergio add the technical nuance:

- Token accounting: we meter per final tokenized character stream sent to the model. If your app expands the JSON array server-side into one consolidated prompt before calling the API, that's billed as one request based on the combined token count. If you call the model multiple times (one call per historical note), each call is billed separately.

- KV/prefix cache: KV entries used internally by runtime to accelerate repeated context don't create additional metering lines — they reduce the per-token compute cost but are not independently charged.

- Streaming & heartbeat: for the pilot we're willing to waive the per-call minimum for pure heartbeat pings (requests with no user-visible output) as long as they don't exceed 1% of overall requests in a given billing period. For regular short prompts, the standard per-request minimum applies.

Sergio, can you add a quick note on how nested JSON gets tokenized and any pitfalls re: tokenization divergence (e.g., different escape rules) so Novamed can decide whether to pre-concatenate or stream individual entries? Camila — I'll follow up with commercial terms for the pilot rounding concession and a short amendment to the SOW if procurement needs it.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks

Hi Eli — technical follow-up. A few engineering bullets so your team can decide implementation approach: 

- Tokenization behavior: we use the same tokenizer as the served model variant. When you send a JSON array as a single string in the prompt, tokenization includes JSON punctuation and any escape characters. That usually compresses well but can sometimes push you over boundary thresholds if there are many small fields.

- Pre-concatenate vs multi-call tradeoff: 
  * Pre-concatenate (single call): simpler accounting (one token bill), prefix cache reuse is less effective across different patient sessions but KV caching can still benefit if repeated prefixes exist. Best when total combined tokens fit comfortably under your latency SLO.
  * Multi-call (one call per note): allows incremental streaming, earlier partial outputs, and more effective micro-caching of repeated note templates, but each call is evaluated independently for per-call minimums and rounding.

- Streaming heartbeat: what we consider a "heartbeat" is a request with no generated tokens in the final response (status-only metadata). These will be excluded from billing if you opt into the pilot waiver and they remain below the 1% volume threshold. Anything that yields >0 generated tokens will be billed and subject to minimums.

- Edge-case: if you send very large nested payloads that cause tokenization to exceed the model's max context, runtime will attempt automatic chunking by default. For billing that results in multiple model calls, you will see multiple line items (one per chunk) unless you choose to pre-chunk and batch on your side — which gives you more control over rounding.

Happy to pair with your engineer for a quick call to look at the CSV you attached.

—Sergio

Eli — commercial follow-up. Per Dylan's note, we're prepared to offer the following for the 30-day pilot (to make procurement sign-off easier):

1) Pilot rounding concession: we'll apply a nightly consolidation credit that will aggregate per-call charges for calls we detect as part of the same session and under 8 token-generation threshold. After consolidation, we'll round down aggregate small-call charges to the nearest whole token-per-session equivalent. This is operational only for pilot customers and will be listed as an SOW addendum.

2) Heartbeat waiver: confirmed — heartbeats (0-token responses) will be excluded from billing up to 1% of total call volume for the pilot period. If Novamed expects a higher heartbeat rate, we can approve a custom waiver but we'd like to understand the use case first.

3) Discounting: we can extend a 12% pilot discount on consumed tokens for the duration of the pilot, applied after any consolidation credits. If you're happy, I can prepare an SOW amendment and DocuSign link.

Attachments: redwood-pricing-summary.pdf (summary of pilot concessions)

If procurement agrees, we'll add the consolidation credit clause into the SOW and map it to DEAL-3891 / HS-3891 for tracking.
